questions.q: How do comparison operators like =, !=, >, and <= behave in SOQL compared to T-SQL?
options: They behave identically to their T-SQL counterparts
SOQL only supports the equals operator
SOQL requires operators to be written as words, e.g. GREATER THAN
Comparison operators are not allowed in SOQL WHERE clauses
questions.explain: SOQL's comparison operators (=, !=, <, >, <=, >=) work exactly like T-SQL's.

questions.q: What do the % and _ wildcards mean in a SOQL LIKE pattern?
options: % matches any number of characters (including zero); _ matches exactly one character
% matches exactly one character; _ matches any number of characters
Both wildcards match exactly one character
SOQL LIKE doesn't support wildcards
questions.explain: SOQL's LIKE wildcards are identical to T-SQL's: % for any number of characters, _ for exactly one.

questions.q: What does the IN operator do in a SOQL WHERE clause?
options: Matches a field's value against any value in a parenthesized, comma-separated list
Checks whether a field is not null
Joins two objects together
Limits the number of records returned
questions.explain: IN matches a field against a list of values, functioning the same way it does in T-SQL; NOT IN excludes matches.

questions.q: In WHERE Amount >= 50000 AND (StageName = 'Proposal' OR StageName = 'Negotiation/Review'), why are the OR conditions wrapped in parentheses?
options: To group them so they're evaluated together before combining with AND, respecting standard operator precedence, same as T-SQL
SOQL requires all conditions to be wrapped in parentheses regardless of logic
Parentheses are purely cosmetic and have no effect on evaluation order in SOQL
Without parentheses, the query would fail to parse entirely
questions.explain: SOQL respects standard operator precedence just like T-SQL, so parentheses control how OR and AND combine.

questions.q: Why is IN often preferable to a chain of OR conditions when filtering a picklist field like StageName?
options: It reads more cleanly while doing the same job, since picklist fields often have several valid values you want to include at once
IN is the only operator that works on picklist fields
OR conditions are not supported at all in SOQL
IN executes faster because it skips governor limits
questions.explain: The lesson notes IN is especially useful for picklist fields with several valid values, reading more cleanly than an OR chain.
